newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GAS COMPANY'S 1996 LOSSES REACH 77 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: GAS COMPANY'S 1996 LOSSES REACH 77 MLN LITAS.

text.p: An offficial with state-run Lithuanian Gas said on Friday that the company had losses of 77 million litas in 1996.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said that the losses stemmed from debts dating back to 1992 and 1993 and from the difference between the price the company paid for supplies and the price paid by its consumers.
The company earlier reported that it had a net profit of 3.9 million litas for 1996 but that sum was not based on audited figures.
The company's profit for 1995 was 43.5 million litas, based Lithuanian accounting standards.
The 1996 audit was based on international accounting standards.
The company earlier said that its shareholders on Monday would discuss a $45 million loan from Merrill Lynch and that it planned to use $20 million to cover past losses.
The company is 90.1 percent state-owned and the remainer of its shares are traded on the Vilnius bourse's A list.
